title: Certutil Used to Decode a Base64 Encoded File
falsepositives: Certutil's legitimate certificate-management usage does not use -decode, so false positives from normal PKI operations are unlikely
description: Detects use of the built-in certutil.exe LOLBin with the -decode flag, a well-known technique for reconstructing an encoded payload on disk while evading naive AV signature checks.
author: DetectForge Team

title: Suspicious Command Shell Invocation Directly From Explorer
falsepositives: Power users who manually type chained commands into an already-open shell (rare from Explorer specifically)
description: Detects cmd.exe launched directly by explorer.exe with a /c command chain, which is unusual since a normal double-click open of Command Prompt starts an interactive shell with no arguments.
author: DetectForge Team

title: LSASS Memory Dump via ProcDump-Style Command Line
falsepositives: Authorized incident-response or forensic memory captures performed by security staff
description: Detects a command line referencing lsass.exe together with a -ma (full memory dump) style flag, consistent with using ProcDump or similar tools to dump LSASS memory for offline credential extraction.
author: DetectForge Team

title: Office Application Spawning Script Interpreter
falsepositives: Legitimate internally-developed mail-merge or document-automation macros that intentionally invoke a script engine (rare, should be allowlisted by specific script path)
description: Detects a Microsoft Office application (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) spawning a script interpreter or shell, commonly seen in malicious macro execution chains such as the OSTap/TrickBot downloader pattern.
author: DetectForge Team

title: Suspicious PowerShell Encoded Command Execution
falsepositives: Legitimate administrative automation scripts using base64 encoded parameters.
description: Detects execution of PowerShell with an encoded command string, which is commonly used by adversaries to obfuscate malicious commands or scripts.
author: DetectForge Team

title: RDP Client Launched Against a Domain Controller
falsepositives: Domain administrators and IT staff legitimately RDP into domain controllers for routine maintenance - tune the hostname pattern to your environment's actual DC naming convention and consider allowlisting known admin accounts
description: Detects mstsc.exe (Remote Desktop client) launched with a target hostname matching common domain-controller naming conventions, which is unusual for a regular workstation user and may indicate lateral movement toward high-value infrastructure.
author: DetectForge Team

title: Registry Modification of SecurityHealth Startup Entry
falsepositives: None expected - legitimate software has no reason to modify this specific value
description: Detects reg.exe adding a value to the SecurityHealth autostart entry, which attackers abuse to replace the Windows Security notification binary with an arbitrary executable.
author: DetectForge Team

title: Persistence via Registry Run Key Addition
falsepositives: Legitimate software installers registering an autostart entry for a user-approved application
description: Detects use of reg.exe to add a new value under the CurrentVersion\Run registry key, a common technique for establishing autostart persistence.
author: DetectForge Team

title: Suspicious Scheduled Task Creation via Schtasks
description: Detects creation of a scheduled task via schtasks.exe, which is commonly used by adversaries for persistence.
author: DetectForge Team

title: System Information Discovery via systeminfo.exe
falsepositives: Legitimate IT inventory, asset-management, and monitoring agents routinely call systeminfo.exe - this rule cannot distinguish that from adversary recon by process creation alone
description: Detects execution of the built-in systeminfo.exe utility, commonly used by adversaries during the discovery phase to profile a compromised host. Note this is an inherently noisy indicator on its own - IT inventory tools and admin scripts also call systeminfo routinely, so this should be correlated with other signals in production rather than alerted on standalone.
author: DetectForge Team

title: UAC Bypass via Event Viewer Registry Hijack
falsepositives: Legitimate registry management tooling that happens to touch the mscfile class (extremely rare)
description: Detects the classic fileless UAC bypass technique that hijacks the mscfile registry class handler (used by eventvwr.msc) to launch an attacker-controlled binary with elevated privileges.
author: DetectForge Team

title: Suspicious Windows Command Shell Redirection Chaining
falsepositives: Legitimate batch scripts that redirect output to a file and then chain a follow-up command
description: Detects cmd.exe invoked with an output-redirection-then-chained-read pattern (write a file, then immediately display it in the same command line), a shape often seen when a command shell is used to stage or verify dropped content.
author: DetectForge Team
